International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

Wildfires across southwestern France and central Spain have forced the evacuation of more than 220,000 people, prompting France to activate the EU's civil protection mechanism and Spain to declare a national emergency [BBC World, France 24, RFI English]. In Ukraine, Russian ballistic missile strikes killed at least 10 people at a drone technology exhibition near Kyiv, with President Zelensky warning of additional massive strikes within 48 hours [BBC World]. The International Criminal Court voted to remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual misconduct allegations, a decision he has vowed to challenge [BBC Europe, Le Monde]. Tensions between the US and EU escalated as President Trump threatened new tariffs and announced a Section 301 investigation in response to European fines on American tech companies [BBC Europe]. Meanwhile, the US-Iran conflict continued for a 13th consecutive night, with both sides signaling potential escalation as oil prices exceeded $100 per barrel [Globe and Mail]. Diplomatic developments included UN Secretary-General Guterres arriving in Syria for the first such visit since before the civil war began [France 24].

ICC Votes to Remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan Over Sexual Misconduct Findings

  • Assembly of States Parties voted 82 in favor to dismiss Khan as ICC chief prosecutor following misconduct investigation
  • Court oversight body found Khan committed 'serious breach of duty' by engaging in improper sexual relationship with junior staff member and attempting to suppress her complaint
  • Khan, elected as ICC's third prosecutor in 2021, was suspended last month; his lawyer said he will challenge the decision through 'all available legal mechanisms'
  • Decision comes amid unprecedented pressure on the court and could reshape the world's only permanent war crimes tribunal
